newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson committed to Great Western deal.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson committed to Great Western deal.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co said Thursday it was still "fully committed" to its merger proposal to Great Western Financial Corp.
Ahmanson criticized Great Western's merger agreement with Washington Mutual Savings Bank. It said it would comment further after it had fully reviewed the details of the pact.
"We are amazed that Washington Mutual's bid is so totally inconsistent with its prior public claims as to how it does acquisitions," a spokesman for Ahmanson said.
The Washington Mutual-Great Western deal does not fit with the strategy on acquisitions that Washington Mutual has discussed in the past, the Ahmanson spokesman said.
The spokesman said his company believed there would be a "negative" reaction in the stock market to the Washington Mutual-Great Western pact.

Ahmanson said Washington Mutual's prediction that a merger with Great Western will result in expense reductions of $340 million (pre-tax) in 1999 was "widely inconsistent" with the cost savings of other transactions of comparable size.
"In particular, these $340 milion of pre-tax cost savings represent approximately 170 pct of the $200 million expense base which Washington Mutual already has in California," it said.
Ahmanson said if Washington Mutual acquires Great Western, it will have expanded its deposit base by an unprecedented 400 percent in 12 months.

"Given the fact that Great Western has never appoached us, we are further amazed by this morning's announcement, particularly in light of the extraordinarily high breakup fee that Great Western is providing with respect to a Washington Mutual transaction," the Ahmanson spokesman said.
